section.title: Cylindrical shells
section.p: Disks and washers came from slices perpendicular to the axis of rotation. A vertical slice rotated around the x-axis made a disk or a washer. A horizontal slice rotated around the y-axis did the same.
But a slice can also be parallel to the axis of rotation.
Then it does not sweep out a disk. It sweeps out a thin cylindrical shell.
The small piece changes shape again:

subsection.title: When shells beat washers
subsection.p: The washer method uses slices perpendicular to the axis of rotation. The shell method uses slices parallel to the axis of rotation.
That one choice can turn a difficult setup into a simple one.

subsection.title: Comparing two methods on the same solid
subsection.p: Different methods should agree when they describe the same solid. The setup may look different, but the volume is the same physical quantity.

note.title: The method is not the meaning
note.p: Shells and washers are two ways to add the same solid. One adds thin cylindrical walls. The other adds thin cross-sectional washers. If both describe the same solid correctly, they give the same volume.
